title: Made 8-direction animations for my game using I2V models
author: Excellent-Treat-7105
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/hresw9otcgoh1.png?width=1536&format=png&auto=webp&s=646be96be435eec759f638a414db74bf33860c6a

https://preview.redd.it/g4vna5bycgoh1.png?width=1024&format=png&auto=webp&s=633686a3f558793e6cbe685cd391e0ae359fa6e2

Been working on 2D character animations for my game using GPT Image and H3 Max. Here's the character running in-game.

I generated the character with GPT Image, made a sheet of it facing all 8 directions, then used image-to-video to animate it. After that, I extracted the frames to use as sprites.

For the video part I used H3 Max, fal's post-trained version of H3. Regular H3 works for this too, but Max is much faster.

https://reddit.com/link/1wbfv3b/video/1bte46s2cgoh1/player

comments.author: Joao_Jacques
comments.body: This is dope! Could you share what kind of prompt you used with minimax h3 for the initial animations? or is that not ok? I knew that minimax was a awesome model for a lot of stuff, but damn!

replies.author: Excellent-Treat-7105
replies.body:
Thanks! Glad you like it :) Happy to share. I didn’t write the prompts myself. I gave Codex instructions on the workflow (generate an 8-direction sprite sheet, then animate it using Minimax H3 i2v), and it wrote the actual prompts.

Codex wrote a pretty long prompt, but I don’t think it needs to be. Just make sure to include two things: keep the facing directions fixed and describe the motion you want.

If you need a loop for something like walking or running, you can also try making the sprite sheet with the character partway through the motion, then using that same sheet as both the first and last frame of the video.

Here’s the prompt Codex wrote:

>Animate this ENTIRE 4-column by 2-row sheet as eight synchronized views of the SAME motion. The camera is fixed high oblique TOP-DOWN, about 60 degrees above the ground. Preserve the source crown, shoulder tops, compact foreshortened bodies and boot tops. Never lower to an eye-level camera.  
>  
>Exactly eight figures stay centered in their original eight cells at the original small size. All heads, feet, cape and sword stay inside their cells, with wide empty green margins. No camera movement, zoom, cropping, cell movement or layout change.  
>  
>Top row: N facing up (back), NE facing upper-right (back-right), E facing right, SE facing lower-right. Bottom row: S facing down (front), SW facing lower-left, W facing left, NW facing upper-left. Each copy moves its limbs toward its own original facing. NEVER turn a head, chest or hips into another direction. In N the mask front is NEVER visible. These are fixed eight views, NOT eight interacting characters.  
>  
>Preserve the ivory pointed mask, dark tunic and trousers, burnt-orange cape, right-handed thin sword, ink outlines and restrained watercolor. No weapon attacks: sword stays safely low at the right side, steady in the hand. No slash trails, particles, shadows, scenery, UI, text or other objects. Solid pure chroma green #00FF00 background throughout. Hand-drawn 2D sprite animation, not a 3D render. Silent.  
>  
>All movement is IN PLACE like on a treadmill. The center of mass and foot-contact center must not translate across the cell. Animate the limbs and cape, not the camera or the entire sprite plate.  
>  
>Perform a clear athletic RUN cycle, visibly different from a walk. Long alternating strides, knees lifting, forceful foot push-off, brief airborne phases, upper body leaning slightly into its facing direction, cape streaming backward. Keep the same top-down camera and small size. From 0.3 to 4.6 seconds sustain six complete rhythmic running cycles, synchronized across all eight views. Start and end in the supplied ready stance. No somersaults, spins or attacks.

replies.author: Joao_Jacques
replies.body: Did you use the max model using an API or running it locally? I dont find the minimax h3 max version anywhere to download. Is the max version only i2va or also ref2va?

replies.author: Excellent-Treat-7105
replies.body:
I used it through fal.ai’s API. It’s discounted until September 14, so it’s pretty cheap right now. Max supports ref2va too:

[https://fal.ai/models/minimax/h3-max/reference-to-video](https://fal.ai/models/minimax/h3-max/reference-to-video)

I also looked into running H3 locally, but was told each generation would take tens of minutes on my setup (RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, 32GB system RAM), so I gave up on that.
